comments.author: @jamesballack4426
comments.text: I help lead the Spanish Banks Streamkeepers (SBSk). Currently doing monitoring of Canyon Creek along with Vancouver Parks Board. Know all about it and can answer your salmon return questions if you're interested. Would love to chat :)

replies.author: @jamesballack4426
replies.text: @HiddenCanada Right now, we're doing water quality monitoring (dissolved oxygen, pH, etc), flow monitoring (ft/s measurements), and temperature measurements. No salmon have been observed yet, but this is just the second possible year for that to happen. Although unlikely, there is a possibility that salmon from other systems may stray and find the creek. Stocking is an option that will likely come to fruition in the next few years. Unfortunately recent DFO mass layoffs have made preparing for this more difficult and the timeline longer out. Realistic return timeline is most likely 5+ years off. A successful restoration would include: heavier riparian growth (creating areas of shade around the creek --> salmon habitat), sufficient water temp/flow/dissolved/oxygen/etc for healthy fish/invertebrate habitat. As far the original project is concerned, that would likely be it, but of course salmon return would be an ideal measurement of success for us.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Absolutely, I’d love to learn more. The biggest thing I couldn’t verify while researching was what monitoring is happening now at Canyon Creek and what a realistic salmon-return timeline looks like. Have any salmon been observed yet, was the creek stocked at all, and what would you consider a successful restoration over the next few years?

replies.author: @HiddenCanada

comments.text: Your review makes me proud to be Canadian. I hope those returning salmon are protected to allow robust recovery. There aren't many bears in the area, but eagles and humans are there. replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Thank you, really appreciate that. And the eagles are actually part of the natural salmon ecosystem, so I don’t think the goal would be to keep them away. Trees and streamside vegetation usually help the creek by providing shade, cover and better habitat for fish. The bigger challenge is making sure the water quality, flow and spawning habitat are good enough for the salmon population to rebuild in the first place.
